book.publisherDescriptionHTML:
• Glossary
  • Dramatis Personae
  • Order of Battle
  • Biographical Apparatus

This is the journal of the Desert March of 1885 and of the last voyage up the Nile to Khartoum, written by Sir Charles William Wilson, head of intelligence of the Nile Expedition. He wrote it up from his daily notes and published it in 1885.

Wilson records the crossing of the Bayuda stage by stage: the wells, the dura, the overloaded camels. He was in the square at Abu Klea and in command at Abu Kru, and he describes both actions with an officer's exactness. He gives the Mahdist Ansar their full due for discipline and courage. In Gordon's own steamers, crewed by Sudanese soldiers, he then forced the river to the junction of the two Niles. He arrived two days after the city had fallen and turned back under fire, through cataracts that wrecked both vessels.

This AETERNUS edition prints the text of the first edition, published by William Blackwood and Sons in Edinburgh and London. It adds a biography of Wilson across his whole life, from the survey of Jerusalem to the Ordnance Survey and the War Office. It also gives his final style and honours, an order of battle drawn from the book's own returns, a dramatis personae of the men who appear in it, a glossary of Sudanese and military terms, and an afterword that sets the campaign on its ground: water, distance and time.
